source.title: Abhinavagupta's argument that vimarśa (reflexive self-awareness) cannot be reduced to structural determination-by-exclusion
source.author: Abhinavagupta (Tantrāloka)

source_span.quote: sa ca viśeṣaḥ svahṛdayagatayā vimarśasattayaivotpadyate — that difference arises as being essentially an act of reflective awareness

claims.claim_text: Mutual distinction (anyonyaviśeṣa) between entities cannot ground itself. Difference requires a prior reflexive awareness (vimarśa) in which it arises. All thirty-six tattvas are equally Light (prakāśa); without vimarśa there would be no basis for differentiating them at all. Determination-by-exclusion operates within vimarśa, not prior to it.
claims.hetu: all tattvas are equally Light, requiring vimarśa for differentiation
claims.sadhya: structural difference presupposes reflexive awareness, not vice versa
claims.vyapti_statement: If differentiation requires reflexive awareness to arise within, then determination-by-exclusion is not foundational but dependent on vimarśa.

falsifier.condition: Demonstrate a case where mutual distinction operates without any prior reflexive awareness — i.e., where A and not-A are determined as distinct without any awareness of the distinction.

claims.reasoning: Direct textual evidence from Tantrāloka 1.52cd. Abhinavagupta explicitly argues that difference (viśeṣa) arises from vimarśa, not prior to it. This directly challenges the claim that determination-by-exclusion is foundational.

source_span.quote: Without vimarśa, consciousness would be insentient, like a crystal

claims.claim_text: Without vimarśa (reflexive self-awareness), consciousness would be insentient like a crystal or mirror — capable of passive reflection but lacking self-presence, life, and awareness. Vimarśa is what distinguishes consciousness from inert luminosity. A mere structural determination-by-exclusion framework cannot account for this qualitative difference between sentient self-presence and insentient reflection.
claims.hetu: a crystal reflects without being aware; vimarśa adds self-presence
claims.sadhya: determination-by-exclusion alone cannot account for the sentient quality of consciousness
claims.vyapti_statement: If structural determination-by-exclusion were sufficient for consciousness, then any system of mutually determined contrasts would be conscious, which is false.

falsifier.condition: Show that a purely structural system of determination-by-exclusion (without any additional reflexive property) exhibits the qualitative character of conscious self-presence — i.e., that it is not merely a system of contrasts but feels like something to be that system.

claims.reasoning: This is Abhinavagupta's decisive argument against reducing consciousness to structure. The crystal argument shows that structure alone (mutual determination, difference, exclusion) does not entail awareness.

source_span.quote: Apoha is not applicable to the light of consciousness that shines everywhere as everything at all times

claims.claim_text: Buddhist apoha (determination-by-exclusion) applies to objective, differentiated entities — to determine 'cow' by excluding 'non-cow'. It does NOT apply to the light of consciousness itself, which is self-luminous, self-present, and not constituted by negation of anything else. Consciousness is not determined by what it excludes; it is self-given. Therefore the formal equivalence between difference and apoha holds at the level of objective determination but does not extend to the nature of consciousness itself.
claims.hetu: consciousness is self-luminous, not determined by negation of other
claims.sadhya: apoha/difference mapping does not apply to the nature of consciousness itself
claims.vyapti_statement: If consciousness is self-luminous and not constituted by negation, then determination-by-exclusion frameworks are inapplicable to consciousness itself, however applicable they may be to objective content.

falsifier.condition: Demonstrate that the self-luminous nature of consciousness can be fully accounted for through determination-by-exclusion — i.e., that 'awareness' is just the exclusion of 'non-awareness' with no remainder.

claims.reasoning: Abhinavagupta explicitly restricts the scope of apoha: it applies to objective entities, not to consciousness itself. This is a scope-limitation argument — the bridge between difference and apoha is valid within its domain but does not extend to the nature of awareness.

source_span.quote: The power of reflective awareness is the inherent freedom of consciousness

claims.claim_text: Vimarśa is the freedom (svātantrya) of consciousness — self-grounding, self-referential, not dependent on any external contrast. Determination-by-exclusion is dependent on others (paratantra): X is 'this' because it is 'not that.' But vimarśa is svatantra: it is not constituted by relation to an other. This categorical difference — dependence on other vs. self-grounding freedom — means vimarśa cannot be reduced to a species of determination-by-exclusion.
claims.hetu: vimarśa is svatantra (self-grounding), determination-by-exclusion is paratantra (other-dependent)
claims.sadhya: vimarśa is categorically different from determination-by-exclusion
claims.vyapti_statement: If vimarśa is self-grounding freedom and determination-by-exclusion is other-dependent, they are categorically different operations even if they co-occur.

falsifier.condition: Show that vimarśa (reflexive self-awareness) can be fully characterized as a determination-by-exclusion operation — i.e., that self-awareness is just the exclusion of non-self-awareness, with no self-grounding remainder.

claims.reasoning: The svātantrya argument is the deepest philosophical point: determination-by-exclusion is constitutively other-dependent, while vimarśa is constitutively self-grounding. This is a categorical distinction, not a matter of degree.

source_span.quote: utpattiś ca tādātmye paryavasyati — difference culminates in oneness

claims.claim_text: Structural determination-by-exclusion terminates in separation: A is A because it is not not-A. But vimarśa culminates in identity (tādātmya): difference is resolved into oneness as the unfolding of the self-aware Heart. The tree-of-vimarśa metaphor — all variegated phenomena are 'sprouts and flowers of the tree of reflective awareness of one's own Self' — shows that vimarśa does not produce separation but expression. This is a fundamentally different structure from determination-by-contrast.
claims.hetu: difference terminates in A ≠ not-A, vimarśa terminates in tādātmya (oneness)
claims.sadhya: vimarśa has a fundamentally different structure from determination-by-exclusion
claims.vyapti_statement: If one operation terminates in separation and another in identity, they are structurally different operations.

falsifier.condition: Show that determination-by-exclusion can also culminate in identity — i.e., that a system of mutual exclusions can resolve into a unified awareness without remainder.

claims.reasoning: This is the culminating argument: difference and vimarśa have opposite directions. Difference produces separation; vimarśa resolves into unity. They cannot be the same operation.
